docs.text: Welcome to your interactive journey into Differential Calculus. Instructions: Type your answer in the boxes below and press ENTER.

docs.title: 🧠 The Concept: Approaching the "Wall"
docs.text:
Imagine walking halfway to a wall, then halfway again. You get closer effectively forever, but mathematically, do you touch it? This is the definition of a Limit (\(L\)).

\[\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n = L\]

docs.title: 👁️‍🗨️ Example: The Infinite Division
docs.text:
Goal: Find the limit of \(a_n = \frac{2n + 1}{n}\) as \(n \to \infty\).

Solution: Divide everything by \(n\): $\(\frac{2n}{n} + \frac{1}{n} = 2 + \frac{1}{n}\)$ Since \(\frac{1}{\infty} \to 0\), the result is 2.

docs.title: 🚀 Challenge 1: Your Turn
docs.text:
Solve for \(a_n = \frac{n+1}{n}\).

Limit ($n \to \infty$):

💡 Stuck? Reveal Solution

Step-by-Step: Divide by \(n\): $\(\lim_{n \to \infty} (1 + 1/n) = 1 + 0 = 1\)$

docs.title: 🧠 The Concept: Limits vs. Values
docs.text: A function can be undefined at a point (like \(0/0\)) but still have a limit. We are looking for the "path", not the destination.

docs.title: 👁️‍🗨️ Example: Removing the Glitch
docs.text:
Goal: \(\lim_{x \to 3} \frac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3}\).

Solution: Factor the top (Difference of squares): $\(\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{(x-3)} = x+3\)$ Now it's safe to plug in \(x=3\). Result is 6.

docs.title: 🚀 Challenge 2: Fix the Function
docs.text:
Find limit of \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 1}{x - 1}\) as \(x \to 1\).

Limit ($x \to 1$):

💡 Stuck? Reveal Solution

Factorize: \((x-1)(x+1)\). Cancel \((x-1)\). Result: \(1+1=2\).

docs.title: 🧠 The Concept: The 0/0 Mystery
docs.text: \(\frac{0}{0}\) is not zero. It means "Do more work". Usually, this means factoring or expanding terms.

docs.title: 👁️‍🗨️ Example: Factoring Out \(x\)
docs.text:
Goal: \(\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{5x^2 + 10x}{x}\).

Solution: Factor out \(x\) from the numerator: \(x(5x+10)\). Cancel \(x\). Limit is \(5(0)+10 = 10\).

docs.title: 🔥 Task A: Sequence
docs.text:
Limit of \(a_n = \frac{3n}{n+2}\)?

Show Solution

Coefficients of highest power: \(3/1 = 3\).

docs.title: 🔥 Task B: Function
docs.text:
Limit of \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 + 3x}{x}\) as \(x \to 0\)?

Show Solution

Simplify to \(x+3\). Limit is \(3\).
